data: Which corpus has a higher mean length of words for words with 9 letters?

The scatter plot shows the mean length of words for two English corpora: one labeled as "Corpus 29.34M Words" and the other as "Corpus DUC'04". The x-axis represents the size of the word in letters, ranging from 1 to 20. The y-axis represents frequency. The lines for both corpora are plotted on the same graph, with the blue line representing "Corpus 29.34M Words" and the red dashed line representing "Corpus DUC'04".

To determine which corpus has a higher mean length of words for words with 9 letters, we need to compare the positions of the two lines at the 9-letter mark on the x-axis. The position of the line indicates the mean length of words for that particular size.

From the scatter plot, it appears that the blue line (Corpus 29.34M Words) is positioned above the red dashed line (Corpus DUC'04) at the 9-letter mark. This suggests that the mean length of words for 9-letter words in "Corpus 29.34M Words" is higher than in "Corpus DUC'04".
Therefore, the answer is "Corpus 29.34M Words".
